links.outcome: Provider use of and negative sentiment toward GPT-4 drafts, engineered vs original prompt
links.effect: Negative sentiment fell from 12.0% to 8.2% (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.36-0.52), but message usage decreased in the mixed model (beta -0.10, 95% CI -0.11 to -0.09, P<.01).
links.quote: In mixed linear regression accounting for the provider and number of messages per provider, the engineered prompt in the post-period was associated with a decrease in message usage (beta coefficient, −0.10; 95% CI, −0.11 to −0.09, P < .01).

links.outcome: Provider uptake and negative sentiment toward AI-generated patient-message drafts
links.effect: Only 1327 (17.5%) of 7605 drafts were used; negative sentiment was 12.0% (n = 468) before and 8.2% (n = 307) after prompt engineering.
links.quote: A total of 7605 draft messages were generated by GPT-4 and 1327 (17.5%) were used as a reply to a patient’s inquiry.

unlisted_practices: Algorithmic prompt optimization using low-perplexity paraphrases, few-shot examples, and self-consistency against expert-generated synthetic reference responses, compared with the original customized prompt.
Extending AI-assisted message drafting to nurse clinicians alongside additional in-servicing and education.

links.effect: 2.6% of generated messages were sent identical or nearly identical to the AI draft.
links.quote: Across all messages, those that were left identical or nearly identical in editing by providers was 2.6% ( n = 202).

links.effect: With additional in-servicing and education, message usage increased to 35.8%.
links.quote: During this period, with additional in-servicing and education, usage increased to 35.8% ( P < .01) with 920 drafted messages used from the 2573 generated.

unlisted_practices: System-level prompt engineering and optimization to improve AI draft quality and reduce negative user sentiment.
